analysis.title: GS flow and positioning observations
key_insights: AI complex sold off hard in Asia on 16 Nov: Taiwan -6%, Korea -3.6%, Nikkei -2.4%, Advantest -11%, Lasertec -9%, Tokyo Electron -7%, Hynix -7.81%, TSMC -5.7%, while Japan domestic consumer names rose 2.75% and healthcare 1.75%. Privorotsky reads AI as beta plus momentum.

Privorotsky says the Nvidia debate is shifting from a tactical hardware share redistribution to whether aggregate AI capex is entering a digestion phase. Nvidia reports Tuesday and he expects it to leave the debate on future AI commitments unresolved.

Rates repriced violently last week: multiple-sigma moves higher in nominal yields and all three Treasury auctions reportedly tailed. PPI was tamer but did not stop the selloff. Credit held up well, which Privorotsky reads as less AI spending meaning lower balance-sheet risk (better credit) but weaker equity multiples.

Prime book flows (Privorotsky): fundamental L/S up just over 1% and quant about 1.5% on the week. Fundamental gross leverage +2.6 pts (34th percentile, 1 year) with net barely changed. Overall PB gross was cut 2 pts, with visible de-grossing in Asia and Europe. HFs net sold US equities for a 2nd straight week (5 of last 6). ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest covering in seven months.

Privorotsky flags an inconsistency: equities price a slowdown while rates price persistent inflation and restrictive policy, and defensives (consumer staples at large forward-earnings premiums) are bid while semis approach historical valuation lows. He asks whether receiving rates is the better expression. Sentiment is depressed (AAII and CNN fear/greed near low ends) and he sees the outcome as a push between challenging macro and positioning.

Pasquariello: equal-weight S&P closed Friday 1% from all-time highs and NDX rallied 3.5% on the week, despite the bellwether AI stock losing over $500bn of market cap and a 33 bps backup in 2-year yields. He sees positive skew of risks through year-end (position cleansing, seasonals with the last seven weeks up 69% of years since 1952 for an average +2.1%, AI demand evidence from TSMC and CRWV, nominal GDP above trend).

Pasquariello expects 2027 to be more complicated: AI buildout path at risk from US politicians, regulation and tax risk, core inflation sticky and broadening in the latest CPI, and 2027 likely sees the largest increase in net supply since 2000. He expects more volatility, less upside convexity and lower risk-adjusted returns, a 'seesaw' market.

Pasquariello's positioning read: since early October the trading community has liquidated a very large amount of risk (net and gross). Last week was the biggest sale of global AI stocks in the franchise since the AI boom began four years ago. PB net exposure is in the 3rd percentile of the past year. Corporate supply-vs-demand should improve through November.

Coppersmith: AI sentiment is about as negative as seen in some time. Tech was the most net-sold sector globally again, and the US Info Tech long/short ratio is the lowest in the PB dataset back to 2016. Flows shifted from long liquidation to more new shorts. The cash desk saw persistent NVDA supply from long-only accounts rotating into hyperscalers and other large-cap tech. CTA positioning in NDX is near max short, so little good news may be needed to spark a squeeze.

Coppersmith: semis have underperformed the S&P by more than 30 points since June, the sharpest relative drawdown since 2002. The GS AI Semis basket (GSCBSMHX) trades at 11x 2028 earnings vs nearly 16x for the S&P, while consensus expects 31% 2028 earnings growth. At the S&P multiple the basket would imply roughly -6% earnings.

Coppersmith: main AI concerns are who funds the added spending and whether enough data centers can be built (state-level restrictions such as Texas). GS Research says 2028 data center capacity additions should be roughly in line with 2027 even in a bearish case, and more than 50% higher if added projects proceed. Financing is the bigger worry as borrowing costs rise; GIR thinks existing NVDA commitments hold but new same-size deals may be harder. NVDA is down 30% and down six weeks in a row. The 2027 Outlook sees AI spending growth peaking early next year. He expects equities to grind higher, wants to be selective, add to AI on weakness rather than chase rallies, and stay disciplined on hedges.

Garrett: the market lacks conviction. 2026 was a year of two halves: H1 returns were Korea +130%, SMH +80%, momentum pair +70%, AI winners +50%, and NDX 2-month Sharpe hit the highest since the late 1990s in June; H2 has seen themes shift from 6-month to 6-day horizons. The vol market is far more convinced than cash that Nov 5 was isolated: the SPX year-end straddle costs less than last Thursday's single-session move.

Garrett PB data: HFs sold US equities in 5 of the last 6 weeks, with long selling outpacing short covering 2.8 to 1 and net exposure in the 2nd percentile (5-year). Globally single stocks have been sold 9 straight weeks while macro product has been bought four straight weeks. US info tech long/short ratio is at a record low (2016 start), the lowest exposure to the largest SPX sector in a decade.

Garrett futures: last Thursday's extreme move surprise ratio triggered vol-control and risk-parity unwinds, with models suggesting about $27bn of SPX supply over a few sessions; they re-risk if vol keeps falling. Brent fell about 20% in 7 sessions in early November (sharpest drawdown ex-COVID), and Thursday's price and open interest action suggest new longs are entering via futures and calls.

Garrett derivatives: there is almost no upside call chasing, so outright long calls are 'not crowded'. Index put/call skew has firmed: a 3m ~5.5% OTM call can be funded by a ~10% OTM put (costless risk reversal), and the 3m 10% OTM put funds 2x 3m 108/118 call spreads. VIX puts traded more volume over the last 10 sessions than at any other point this year, and the VIX Dec 18/16 1x2 put spread costs about 0.50 (UX2 ref 19.4).

Garrett: implied-realized vol spread is at its widest negative in over a year and negative for every US sector except utilities, meaning options treat the vol spike as a one-off. The SPX year-end straddle costs 4.2% vs last Thursday's -4.4% move, and the NDX year-end straddle costs 6.8% vs -6.4%.

Garrett baskets: 12m momentum (GSPRHIMO) had its best outperformance vs 3m momentum (GSPRHMO3) in the records, more AI names are in the short leg of 3m momentum, and momentum positioning has collapsed so consensus winners are no longer crowded. US long/short net exposure (Wall St) is diverging from AAII equity exposure (Main St), showing undaunted retail participation (AAII data through 31 Oct).

Week ahead: Nvidia earnings Tuesday, US retail sales Tuesday, HD Tuesday, TGT/LOW/TJX Wednesday, WMT Thursday, FOMC minutes Wednesday, Fed speakers including Williams and Warsh Monday, and possible Trump/Xi/Putin engagement at the APEC summit later in the week. Privorotsky expects low odds of meaningful progress on geopolitics.

Europe: Burnham speaks before the UK/EU summit (trade, carbon markets, youth mobility), with UK employment and CPI the near catalysts amid weak growth and stubborn inflation. France's social security financing bill faces a Senate vote Wednesday after rejection in the National Assembly. For OATs the question is whether a credible fiscal adjustment survives parliament.

market_movers.rationale: Stock is down 30% and down six weeks in a row, with persistent long-only supply. Earnings Tuesday are a watershed for AI sentiment, though GIR thinks existing commitments hold and new same-size deals may be harder.
TSMC fell 5.7% in Asia on 16 Nov amid the AI complex selloff, though Pasquariello also cites TSMC as evidence AI demand remains strong.

Most net-sold sector globally with a record-low US info tech long/short ratio, and CTAs near max short NDX, so a squeeze is possible. Desk wants to be selective.
Staples command large forward-earnings premiums while nominal and real yields are not falling, which Privorotsky finds inconsistent.
Demand is building in energy commodities after Brent fell about 20% in 7 sessions, with new longs entering futures and calls.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reports Tuesday (per the note, no estimate figures given). Privorotsky expects it to reinforce that the stock is heavily discounted on next year's numbers, but the right multiple for 2028 and beyond is unknowable.
GS AI Semis basket: consensus expects 31% earnings growth in 2028 (consensus estimate, not a print). At the S&P's roughly 16x multiple, current prices would imply about -6% earnings.
Retail earnings this week: HD Tuesday, TGT, LOW and TJX Wednesday, WMT Thursday. Privorotsky says to watch trade-down, margins and whether the defensive premium is justified.

tension_points.bull_case: Even in a bearish scenario 2028 data center capacity additions are roughly in line with 2027, and could be more than 50% higher if added projects proceed. The AI semis basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings vs 16x for the S&P with consensus 2028 growth of 31%, and positioning is washed out (CTAs near max short NDX).
tension_points.bear_case: AI spending growth could peak early next year, financing is getting more expensive, and new NVDA deals of the same size may be harder to arrange. Privorotsky sees possible digestion of aggregate AI capex, which would hurt equity multiples more than GDP.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A digestion phase in aggregate AI enterprise capex, or Nvidia earnings Tuesday that show new commitments failing to materialize.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is cleansed, seasonals are strong after the midterms, nominal GDP is accelerating, and equal-weight S&P is 1% from highs.
tension_points.bear_case: Sticky and broadening core inflation, violent rates repricing, tailing auctions, and AI leadership under pressure leave no clear driver for a sustained recovery.
